page.layout: One page of text in a single main column; in the left margin three notes beside the first lines of the column, one of them with a catchword-like running head beside "DAMMONA". Running head at top right above the text. Page number at top left. Below the last line a catchword "tuum" at the lower right.

main_text.p: de qua nunc scribimus potissimum, universæ regionis nunc descriptæ, vt & totius Drentiæ commune velut horreum.

Aggeres flu-ctibus oppo-siti.Regio universa ab exitu Lavicæ per ambages varias, quà æstuarium se curvat, quà Hunesius egredитur, quà vadum à septentrionib. alluit, quà Ámasus, quà Dullartus se sinuant, in ora aggerib. perpetuis, opere difficillimo, sepitur & defenditur contra aquarum influxum: idemq;, vt dixi jam ante, secundum Hunesi lapsum fit non ab urbe solum, sed & supra urbem, usq; ad ejusdem ostium. In ea post Groningam nobilissima & maxima DAMMONA.DAMMONA est, non vilis oppidi instar, si ambitum, & frequentiam habitatorum, si ædificiorum numerum, magnitudinem, formam, si viarum habitum speciem, sed honore mœnium, & jure imperii civilis magistratuum carens, amœna, in circulum fere se colligens, fosaq; ut plurimum cingens, teplo illustri cum turre late spectabili insignis; fanum quoq; monasticum peramplum, sed extra ambitum, lateri tamen occiduo pene contiguum habens familiam Augustinianam, nunc ab omni cultu desertum, ac vix se sustinens: sita ad Fivelam amnem duab. infra Groningam milliaribus caeciam versus, eodemq; amne navigabili media divisa, pontibus intus conexa quinq;: unde ad exitum amnis, ubi Delffilæus portus & castellum, milliare dimidium: vallo, fossa, portis quondam munita ab Edsardo ante annos centum, & triennio post à Georgio Saxone civitatis quoq; jure atq; ordine magistratuum

page.notes: The left margin notes read "Aggeres flu-", "ctibus oppo-", "siti." and "DAMMONA." Two words in the main text are printed in a mixed or doubtful form ("egredитur" contains a Cyrillic-looking letter and should read "egreditur"; the text "Ámasus" is uncertain). Lines near the bottom are faint. The final line "tuum" is printed as the catchword and also as the last word of the text; it is kept only in the catchword position to avoid duplication. Some letters in the margin are hard to read and may be imprecise.
